feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 0 (4 cm span, 12 mm sensors, y 0.05, mass 0.8) lost the line 1.0 to 2.0 times per run and scored 52.28, the best so far. Iterations 1 to 4 each changed one lever (span, forward offset y 0.04 to 0.03, mass 0.7 to 0.6 kg, wheel_radius 0.03 to 0.035 m), and line_loss_events stayed at 1.0 per run on all three tracks in every case. Steering oscillation stayed between 0.07 and 0.14, so the robot is not jittering. Progress has been the main driver of score, and the iteration 1 to 4 sensing and dynamics changes lowered it on the oval and s-bend. Because wheel_track 0.16 m is the last untested turn-authority lever, the Integrator built it with the controller held fixed. Decision rules for the next race: (1) If line_loss_events fall to 0.5 or below on s-bend and slalom and max_error stays under 0.06 m, keep wheel_track 0.16 m and check whether progress rises above the iteration 4 values. (2) If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, the wider track is overshooting; return wheel_track to 0.14 m. (3) If line_loss_events stay at 1.0 per run, geometry is not the limit for this loss. Return to the iteration 0 sensing (5 sensors, 12 mm, y 0.05 m, span ±2 cm), which gave the best score, and look for a fixed point on the course.
requested_changes: Keep wheel_track at 0.16 m with wheel_radius 0.035 m, mass 0.6 kg and the seven-sensor ±3 cm, y 0.03 m, 16 mm layout. Basis: iterations 1 to 4 left line loss at 1.0 per run under every sensing, mass and radius change, so track width is the remaining turn-authority test.

If line loss persists at 1.0 with wheel_track 0.16 m, revert the sensing to the iteration 0 layout (five 12 mm sensors at x -0.02 to +0.02, y 0.05 m) with mass 0.8 kg. Basis: iteration 0 scored 52.28, the best result, with the same 1.0 to 2.0 line-loss pattern, and the progress gap in later iterations has come from the sensing changes.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 at wheel_track 0.16 m, try wheel_track 0.14 m again with mass 0.6 kg. Basis: oscillation was 0.07 to 0.14 across iterations 0 to 4, so there is room, but a wider track increases yaw rate and could overshoot.
